proof_nl: Let x be an arbitrary real number. By definition, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. In particular, floor(x) itself is an integer that does not exceed x, so floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Directly from the defining property of the floor function: floor(x) is the greatest integer ≤ x, hence floor(x) ≤ x for all real x.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly restates the defining property of the floor function and concludes floor(x) ≤ x for arbitrary real x. It is complete, matches the lemma exactly, and uses only legal foundational reasoning.
